title: The Hadacol tours and their collapse
summary: Sharkey describes the Hadacol medicine shows of 1951-52, the lavish train, and how the promoter went bankrupt owing everyone.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: they should have made more. Yeah, yeah. Well, another trip of yours I just thought of last night was going to ask you about that Hadacall trip. I guess they still owe you money for that, do they?

Yeah. Now, that was a fabulous thing, Bill. Yeah, I never... The first, the first show, there were two shows. Yeah. Now, the first show, they traveled in bus, big bus, Greyhound bus. They'd take all the performers and the entertainer and the musician.
When was that? I forget, was that in the 40s?
No, no, it was 1951. That late?
And then they had another one in 1952.
Now, that was the one where they went bankrupt. Yeah. And he sold the Hadacall company to some other medical...
Do they still make the stuff? I don't remember seeing it ever. Yes, they make it. It's on the market. It's still on the market. I wasn't sure. Yeah.

In other words, he over-promoted himself. Yeah, he must have. Now, he could have made a lot of money, but in other words, he would hire... The last show they had, he had a 16-coach train. Oh, yeah. That's good. Now, that's a lot of money.
And everybody on the show could go in the diner and eat and just sign a tale. Yeah. It was marvelous for the entertainers and the help, but he could... It was too expensive.
Yeah, finally got too much. Yeah.

So, we finally got to Dallas and that was the end. And not only did he owe me money, he owes everybody... I guess everybody. ...that was on the show. Jimmy Durante, Milton Boyle, and... They were all on that show. Count Carmen Miranda, Dick Haynes. He owes them all money. Yeah, he had the biggest things. The electricians, the sound equipment, the carpenters, they all got it.
